### Rename people-hub to crm

One mechanical step, first, so everything after it is written in the new vocabulary:

- `packages/people-hub/` → `packages/crm/`, and the package name `@cyc-seattle/people-hub` →
  `@cyc-seattle/crm`. `pnpm-workspace.yaml` globs `packages/*`, so only `pnpm-lock.yaml` needs
  regenerating.
- `docs/people-hub-schema.md` → `docs/crm-schema.md`, including its `tags:` front matter.
- `packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/people-hub.ts` → `crm.ts`, the import in `index.ts:10`,
  the `peopleHubSchema` export, and the schema path at `people-hub.ts:55`.
- Prose references in `docs/architecture.md:176`, `docs/manual-setup.md:113`,
  `packages/substrate/deploy/docker-compose.yml:55`, `directus.ts:18`, `directus.ts:36`,
  `directus.ts:160`, `directus.ts:311`, `directus-client.ts:122`, `substrate-apply.ts:23`, and
  `CLAUDE.md`.

**The Pulumi resource names cost the most care.** A resource name is part of its URN, so renaming
`people-hub-schema`, `people-hub-staff`, `people-hub-coach`, `people-hub-guardian`, and
`people-hub-staff-ungood` makes Pulumi create the new resource and delete the old one. For
`DirectusSchema` the delete is a no-op by design (`directus.ts:144`), so that one is safe either
way. `DirectusRole` and `DirectusUser` are not: their deletes really do call
`DELETE /roles/{id}`, `DELETE /policies/{id}`, and `DELETE /users/{id}`
(`directus.ts:266-280`, `directus.ts:353-356`). Deleting the Staff role would strip the role from
any Directus user assigned to it in the UI, not just the one Pulumi manages.

`pulumi.Alias` is the right answer. Add `aliases: [{ name: "people-hub-staff" }]` (and so on) to
each renamed resource's options. Pulumi then treats the old URN in state as the same resource and
performs no create or delete. Aliases work for dynamic resources because the resource type
(`pulumi-nodejs:dynamic:Resource`) does not change — only the name does. Keep the aliases in the
code after the rename applies. Removing them later is safe but is not worth a commit.

Verify with `just preview` before `just deploy`. The preview must show no creates and no deletes
for the five renamed resources.

### Where the sync code lives

A new package, `packages/clubspot-sync`. It depends on `clubspot-sdk` and `commodore` only — no
`gsuite`, no `googleapis`. The dependency graph is unchanged in direction.

`admin-functions` is not the right home. It keeps `roster.ts`, which genuinely needs Sheets and
Drive (`packages/admin-functions/src/roster.ts:2`), and it pulls in `google-spreadsheet` and
`googleapis`, which the sync never needs. `packages/people-hub/README.md:5` already sets the
precedent that a second Directus-backed app is its own package.

The package contains a small Directus REST client (static-token auth, `GET /items`, `POST /items`,
`PATCH /items`). It does not import
`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus-client.ts` — an app must not depend on the
deployment package. That duplicates about 40 lines of `fetch` plumbing. Extracting a shared
`packages/directus` package that both use is the larger refactor. It is not part of this plan.

The sync sends no Google Chat notifications. It writes failures to the sync log and exits non-zero.
Notifications, and which package `notifications.ts` should live in, get their own issue.

### Shape of the sync

Follow `roster.ts`: a pure function builds a plan, a thin executor writes it. For each collection
the sync reads every existing row once (`GET /items/<collection>?limit=-1`), keys them by
`clubspot_*_id`, and computes creates and updates against the Clubspot objects. That makes the
whole mapping layer unit-testable with no Directus.

Two passes, with different rules:

- **Schedule** (`programs`, `sessions`, `classes`, `session_classes`, `entry_caps`) — full
  reconcile per camp, not watermark-filtered. `sessions.ts:56` already does this, for the same

  `session_classes` expands Clubspot's `allClasses` flag into explicit rows, per
  `docs/crm-schema.md`'s session_classes section.
- **Registrations** (`people`, `contacts`, `medical_profiles`, `registrations`,
  `registration_billing`, `registration_entries`, `custom_field_responses`) — filtered on
  `updatedAt` between the watermark and the run start, the same interval logic as `reports.ts:42`.

Entry removal gets a real fix. When a session is removed from a registration, Clubspot drops the
join object, so the current code marks every row for that participant "cancelled" first, then
rewrites the survivors (`participants.ts:111`). The hub version fetches the existing
`registration_entries` for that registration and sets `status = cancelled` on any whose
`clubspot_session_join_id` is gone. No global pre-pass.

### What the job syncs, and when

There is no config collection and no `enabled` toggle. The job syncs everything for one club. The
club id comes from a `CLUBSPOT_CLUB_ID` environment variable on the Cloud Run job, the same shape

club id comes from a `CLUBSPOT_CLUB_ID` environment variable on the Cloud Run job, the same shape
as `CONFIG_SPREADSHEET_ID` today (`run-reports-job.ts:78`) and already an established variable name
in the SDK CLI (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/main.ts:128`).

Each run:

1. List every non-archived `Camp` for the club, as `camps.ts:37` already does.
2. For each camp, decide whether anything changed since that camp's own watermark. A camp's
   `updatedAt` does not move when a child object changes, so the camp is checked with one
   `Parse.Query.count()` per child class, each filtered on `updatedAt >= watermark`: `CampSession`,
   `CampClass`, `Registration`, and `RegistrationCampSession`. If every count is zero and the
   camp's own `updatedAt` is older than the watermark, skip the camp.
3. Sync each camp that changed, and record one log row per camp.

Two known holes in step 2, both closed by the same rule:

- `EntryCap` has no pointer to a camp (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:338-342`), so a
  capacity-only change is invisible to the count queries.
- Nothing in Clubspot's `updatedAt` reveals a delete.

So any camp whose last successful sync is more than 24 hours old is synced regardless of the
counts. That is a refresh floor, not a snooze.

**Snooze is premature.** The cost the user is worried about is four `count()` calls per camp per
run. With tens of camps and an hourly schedule that is a few hundred cheap queries a day, against
the thousands of object reads a full pass costs. Add a snooze when a measurement says it is needed.

### The sync log

Two append-only collections replace the config worksheet. They hold status and, between them, the
watermark.

**sync_runs** — one row per job execution.

| Field                                 | Notes                                  |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `id`                                  | primary key                            |
| `started_at`                          | timestamp, set at the start of the run |
| `finished_at`                         | timestamp, nullable until the run ends |
| `status`                              | string: `running`, `ok`, `failed`      |
| `programs_checked`, `programs_synced` | integer                                |
| `error`                               | text, nullable                         |

**sync_program_runs** — one row per camp the run touched.

| Field                            | Notes                                                  |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`                             | primary key                                            |
| `run_id`                         | FK to `sync_runs`                                      |
| `program_id`                     | FK to `programs`, nullable on the first sync of a camp |
| `clubspot_camp_id`               | string, so a failed first sync still identifies itself |
| `started_at`, `finished_at`      | timestamp                                              |
| `status`                         | string: `ok`, `failed`, `skipped`                      |
| `items_created`, `items_updated` | integer                                                |
| `error`                          | text, nullable                                         |

**The watermark is per camp, not per run**: the greatest `started_at` among that camp's
`sync_program_runs` rows with `status = ok`, or the epoch if there are none. A run-level watermark
would lose data — if camp A succeeds and camp B fails in the same run, a run-level watermark would
advance past B's missed window. Use the run's `started_at`, not `finished_at`, so a Clubspot write
made during the run is picked up next time. `runner.ts:120` already gets this right today.

Retention is not designed here. The log grows by roughly one row per camp per hour. Revisit when it
is large enough to matter.

### Person identity

Pointers run from the registration-specific rows to `people`, and they are resolved **once, when
the row is created**. `registrations.person_id` is the participant. `contacts.person_id` is a
guardian or an emergency contact. On every later run the sync leaves an existing row's `person_id`
alone. It never re-resolves.

That is the whole reason a manual merge is durable. Staff repoint the FK, delete the loser, and no
later sync undoes it.

**Matching at creation.** Directus's REST filters give `_eq` and `_icontains` and nothing else —
there is no trigram or similarity operator over REST. So "fuzzy" means normalize, fetch a small
candidate set with an indexable filter, and compare in the client:

1. Normalize: trim, lowercase, collapse inner whitespace, strip punctuation from names. Normalize
   phone numbers to digits only.
2. Fetch candidates. With an email:
   `GET /items/people?filter[email][_eq]=<email>`. Without one:
   `GET /items/people?filter[last_name][_icontains]=<last name>&limit=50`.
3. Match in the client, by kind:
   - **Participant** — same normalized first and last name, and the same `date_of_birth`. If the
     participant has no date of birth, require the same normalized email as well.
   - **Guardian** — same normalized email and same normalized last name. Allow an edit distance of
     one on the first name, which catches a typo but not "Bob" against "Robert".
   - **Emergency contact** — same normalized full name and same normalized phone. Clubspot gives
     emergency contacts no email at all (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:373`), so there is
     nothing stronger to match on.
4. No match creates a new `people` row.

The matcher is deliberately reluctant. A false split makes a duplicate that staff merge in a minute.
A false merge silently attaches one family's registration to another person's record, and the data
it corrupts is medical and emergency data. When in doubt, create.

An email alone is never a match. Families share one address, so `parentGuardianEmail` and
`parentGuardianEmail_secondary` are often the same string for two different adults.

**Field updates on an existing person** fill gaps only. If `people.email` is null and the
registration has one, write it. If it already holds a value, leave it. That keeps a staff edit, and
a merge, from being overwritten by the next registration that names the same person.

**The manual merge task** is a Directus UI procedure, documented in `docs/crm-schema.md`:

1. Open the duplicate person.
2. Read the three reverse lists on the person detail page to find every row that points at them.
3. Repoint each row's person field at the person being kept.
4. Delete the duplicate.

Step 2 needs two more alias fields on `people`, alongside the `guardian_links` one that already
exists for `contacts.related_person_id` (`people-hub.ts:105`): one reversing `contacts.person_id`
and one reversing `registrations.person_id`. Alias fields add no columns.

### Schema changes

One regeneration of `packages/crm/schema.yaml` against a live instance covers all of them.

| Collection                                           | Change                                                                                                                                                             | Why                                                                                                                                |

`cartObject`, `customer`, and `stripeAccount` are not modeled. They are Stripe plumbing, not
reporting data.

This changes `docs/crm-schema.md`, which currently says billing stays out of scope. Update that
section rather than leaving the doc contradicting the schema.

### Custom fields, weight, and school

`Participant` has no `weight` and no `school` field. What it has is
`customFieldsArray?: CustomFieldResponse[]` (`types.ts:365`), holding `{ customFieldID, response }`
pairs (`types.ts:353`). The definitions live on the camp as `customFieldsArray?: CustomField[]`
(`types.ts:224`). `Camp.collect_weight` (`types.ts:221`) is a form flag, not a value. So weight and
school almost certainly arrive as custom-field responses.

**`CustomField` has no reverse-engineered attributes** (`types.ts:102-109` is a bare
`Parse.Object`). Without its label field there is no way to tell which response is the weight.
**Issue #90 does not cover this** — it scopes Events, Communication, e-signatures, and accounting.
So reverse-engineering `customFields` is a step in this plan, not a dependency on #90. The existing
generic CLI does it: `clubspot customFields get <id>` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/main.ts:109`)
against an id taken from a camp's `customFieldsArray`.

Model it as two collections, not a JSON blob:

**custom_field_definitions** — `id`, `program_id` (FK to `programs`), `label`, `field_type`,
`clubspot_custom_field_id` (unique).

**custom_field_responses** — `id`, `registration_id` (FK to `registrations`), `definition_id` (FK
to `custom_field_definitions`), `value` (text).

filter, sort, or display inside one without a custom interface, and the reason to capture weight
and school at all is to put them on a roster and filter by them.

### Authentication to Directus

The job authenticates with a Directus static token held by a machine user.

1. `randomSecret("clubspot-sync-directus-token")` in `directus.ts` generates the value and stores
   it in Secret Manager.
2. `DirectusUser` gains an optional `token` input. It provisions OIDC users only today — `provider`
   and `external_identifier`, no password and no token

# Implement a Task

Hand one scoped change to a sub-agent. The sub-agent edits, verifies, and commits. You review the result.

The sub-agent starts cold. It knows nothing about the session, the previous tasks, or the conversation. Everything it needs goes in the brief.

## 1. Prepare the brief

Find the exact `path:line` anchors yourself before you write the brief. A brief that names a file and a line is worth far more than one that describes a symptom.

## 2. Dispatch

Use `Agent` with `subagent_type: implementer`.

The agent already knows the conventions, the test pattern, the `just` rules, and the git rules — they are in `.claude/agents/implementer.md`. Do not repeat them. The brief carries only what is specific to this task:

**Task.** What to change, concretely, with `path:line` anchors.

**Scope fence.** The exact boundary of this change. Name anything adjacent it must not touch.

**Context it cannot derive.** A decision already made, a constraint from the design doc, a reason the obvious approach is wrong. If an approved design doc covers this step, give its path and the step number.

**Never ask for a comment.** Give the agent the constraint and let the standing rule in `CLAUDE.md` decide whether it earns a comment. A brief that says "leave a comment explaining why" overrides that rule, and the agent will write five lines where none were needed.

**Acceptance.** How to know the change worked — the behavior that should differ, or the test that should now pass.

## 3. Review the result

1. Run `git show --stat HEAD`. Read the full diff if the change is non-trivial.
2. Check that the diff stayed inside the scope fence.
3. Summarize for the user in two or three lines: what changed, whether the checks passed, and anything the sub-agent flagged.

If the work is wrong or too wide, dispatch a follow-up sub-agent or run `git revert`. Do not patch it by hand — that defeats the point of delegating.

## Rules

- One writing sub-agent at a time. Two will collide on the shared working tree.
- One commit per task. A bad task can then be reverted without unpicking the batch.

input.prompt:
Step 4 of the approved design doc at `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`. Create the new `packages/clubspot-sync` package containing only its Directus REST client and that client's unit tests. Read the doc's "Where the sync code lives" section (around line 57) first.

Steps 2, 3, and 5-12 are NOT part of this task. You are building an empty package plus one well-tested module.

## Task

**Create `packages/clubspot-sync`** following the layout every other package uses. `packages/calendar-sync/package.json` and `packages/calendar-sync/tsconfig.json` are the closest templates.

- Name `@cyc-seattle/clubspot-sync`, version `0.0.1`, ESM (`"type": "module"`), Apache-2.0, author "CYC Community Sailing Center", `main`/`types` pointing into `dist`, the same `prepare`/`build`/`clean` scripts.
- Dependencies: `@cyc-seattle/commodore` (`workspace:^`) and `winston`. Add `@cyc-seattle/clubspot-sdk` too — later steps need it and declaring it now keeps the dependency graph honest. Do NOT add `@cyc-seattle/gsuite`, `googleapis`, or `google-spreadsheet`; the whole point of a separate package is that the sync never pulls those in.
- For `engines.node`, use `">= 20.8 < 23"` as `calendar-sync` does. Do not copy `clubspot-sdk`'s `< 21` bound — CLAUDE.md records it as a known mistake.
- `tsconfig.json` extends `../../tsconfig.json` with `rootDir: "./src"`, `outDir: "./dist"`, `include: ["src/**/*"]`.
- Tests go in `packages/clubspot-sync/test/**/*.test.ts` — a top-level `test/` directory, not co-located. `vitest.config.ts` already globs `packages/*/test/**/*.test.ts`, so it needs no change.

**Write `src/directus.ts`** — a small REST client for Directus's Items API, authenticated with a static bearer token.

Model it closely on `packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus-client.ts`, which solves the same problems: the `HttpResponse` interface and `httpFetch` wrapper at `:11-20` exist because this repo's tsconfig resolves the ambient `fetch`/`Response` types to an empty structural type, and `directusRequest` at `:57-73` shows the error-handling and 204 shape. Reproduce that approach.

**Do not import from `packages/infrastructure`.** An application package must not depend on the deployment package. The design doc settles this at lines 67-71 and accepts the ~40 lines of duplication; extracting a shared `packages/directus` is explicitly out of scope.

The client differs from the infrastructure one in two ways: it authenticates with a static token supplied at construction (not an email/password login), and it works with items rather than schema.

Operations to support:

- `readItems<T>(collection, query?)` — `GET /items/<collection>`. The query needs at least `filter`, `limit`, `fields`, and `sort`. Directus takes filters as `filter[field][_operator]=value` query parameters; build that encoding here and test it, since later steps depend on `_eq` and `_icontains` for person matching. Support `limit: -1` (Directus's "all rows").
- `createItems<T>(collection, items)` — `POST /items/<collection>`. Directus accepts an array for a batch create; use that rather than one request per row.
- `updateItem<T>(collection, id, patch)` — `PATCH /items/<collection>/<id>`.

Two behaviors that matter to later steps and should be designed in now rather than retrofitted:

- **Pagination.** Directus caps a default page. `limit: -1` returns everything, but a large collection read is where this will first hurt. Either return everything transparently by following pages, or make the cap explicit in the signature — pick one and make the choice legible in the types.
- **A dry-run mode.** Step 9 adds a `--dry-run` CLI flag, and the doc treats it as the primary safety mechanism for the first production run. Give the client a constructor flag that makes every write a no-op returning what it would have written, and log at `winston.info`. Reads always execute.

**Unit tests** in `packages/clubspot-sync/test/`. `packages/infrastructure/test/directus-client.test.ts` is the model — it stubs the global `fetch` with `vi.stubGlobal` and a `jsonResponse` helper (`:16-23`), and calls `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` in `afterEach`. Cover: the filter-to-query-string encoding for `_eq` and `_icontains`, `limit: -1`, the bearer token reaching the Authorization header, a non-OK response producing an error that names the status and the path, the 204/empty-body case, batch create sending one request, and dry-run mode issuing no write request while still allowing reads.

## Scope fence

- Create no other source file. No mapping code, no CLI, no `main.ts`, no sync logic — those are steps 5 through 9.
- Do not modify `packages/infrastructure` in any way, including `directus-client.ts`.
- Do not modify `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `vitest.config.ts`, `Dockerfile`, or anything under `packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap`.
- Do not update `CLAUDE.md`'s package list or dependency graph — that is step 12.
- Do not write the package README — that is also step 12.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes: install, build, check, and test.
- The new tests run and pass under `just test`.
- `packages/clubspot-sync/package.json` has no dependency on `googleapis`, `google-spreadsheet`, `@cyc-seattle/gsuite`, or `@cyc-seattle/infrastructure`.
- `grep -rn "infrastructure" packages/clubspot-sync/src` returns nothing.

Commit once.

Thank you for registering for summer sailing camp at the CYC Community Sailing Center! We’re excited to have them join us on the water for a fun and educational experience.

  • Time: 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM (except for Teen Adventure, which includes an overnight trip on Wednesday)
  • Location: Corinthian Yacht Club, Shilshole Bay Marina

As we get closer to the start of camp, we’ll send you a detailed email with everything you need to know, including a packing list, drop-off and pick-up instructions, and other important information. In the meantime, you can review our Frequently Asked Questions for details on what to bring, safety policies, and more.

If you are interested in learning how to sail as well, please check out our Adult Learn-to-Sail classes on our Adult Sailing Classes page. We'd love to have you out on the water with us!

Lastly, if you have any questions before then, feel free to reach out to us at info@cyccommunitysailing.org or call us at (206) 402-6870.

We can’t wait to see your child on the water this summer!

Kind regards,
Jack

--

Jack Killalea
Sailing Director
CYC Community Sailing Center

Thank you for registering for CYC Community Sailing Center's Summer Sailing Camp!

If you have any issues or questions, please reach out to info@cyccommunitysailing.org.

In addition to contact information which will be used to communicate event information with you and/or the participant, we also collect health information to be used in the event of a medical emergency and additional, optional, information which is used to help us identify areas to grow our programs and evaluate progress against our DEI goals. Please see our Privacy Policy and Non-Descrimination Policy for more details.

Cancellation and Refund Policy - All Programs

  • Within 48 hours of registration: 100% refund.

  • 30 or more days before the program start date: 80% refund.

  • 14 to 30 days before the program start date: 50% refund.

  • Under 14 days before the program start date: no refund will be given.

  • All refunds exclude processing fees.

We reserve the right to cancel programs without a minimum number of participants. For cancelled programs, we will make every attempt to place participants in an alternate program and, if unable, will issue a 100% refund.

Auth unblocked step 2, and going to the live API instead of trusting the SDK types paid off — **three of the design's claims were wrong.**

**`weight` is a real participant field**, populated on 118 of 168 camp participants, stored as a numeric string. Not a custom field at all. The SDK's `ParticipantAttributes` simply never listed it, which is what led the designer astray.

**`pcpName` and `pcpNumber` exist**, so `medical_profiles.physician_name`/`physician_phone` have a source rather than staying permanently null. CYC has used them once in 168, so expect them empty — but the mapping is now correct.

**Emergency contacts do have an email**, plus an entire secondary contact set (`emergencyContact_secondary` and friends). All missing from the SDK type. They're barely used — `emergencyEmail` is filled on 1 of 168 — so the name+phone match rule survives, but as a fallback rather than the only possibility.

Other findings worth knowing:

- **School is a custom field**, the most common one: 24 camps carry a `text` field named exactly `School`.
- **`gender` is populated on 168 of 168** despite `collect_gender` being false on every camp. You were right to want it.
- **A custom field's label is `name`, and it can run to thousands of characters** — one is an entire NWISA code of conduct. That column has to be `text`, not `varchar`.
- **Definitions are per camp and drift across clones.** "School" exists as 24 distinct objectIds linked by `cloned_from`, and labels mutate — "Race / Ethnicity" on 22 camps, "Race/Ethnicity" on 6. Grouping the same logical question across camps is a reporting problem, not a sync one, so the doc no longer pretends to solve it.
- Responses carry an `optionObjectID` for select/radio answers that the SDK type omits, and `customFieldOptions` is a whole class the SDK doesn't register.

Corrections committed as `0d5406f6`. Steps 1 and 4 are in (`4bed92b7`, `42dad040`) — the rename, and `packages/clubspot-sync` with its Directus client and 12 passing tests.

Next is step 2 proper: adding these fields to the SDK's types so later steps can read them. I have everything needed to brief it precisely. Want me to keep going?
Yes, keep going.

input.prompt:
Step 2 of the approved design doc at `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`. Type the `customFields` Parse class and the participant fields the SDK is missing, in `packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts`. Read the doc's "Custom fields, weight, and school" section (around line 279) first — it records these findings.

This is a types-only change. No new behavior, no new commands.

## Context you cannot derive

Every attribute below was read off the **live** Clubspot API against CYC's club (50 camps, 168 camp participants), not inferred. Do not "correct" them against the existing types — the existing types are the thing that was wrong. Do not try to query Clubspot yourself; you have no credentials, and you do not need them.

## Task

**1. `CustomField` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:102-109`)** is currently a bare `Parse.Object` with no attributes. Give it a real `CustomFieldAttributes` interface:

| Attribute              | Type                       | Notes                                                        |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `name`                 | `string`                   | the label. NOT `label`                                       |
| `type`                 | `string`                   | observed: `text`, `select`, `radio`, `file_upload`           |
| `required`             | `boolean`                  |                                                              |
| `hide_from_member`     | `boolean`                  |                                                              |
| `allClasses`           | `boolean`                  | when false, `campClassesArray` scopes which classes see it   |
| `campClassesArray`     | `CampClass[]`, optional    |                                                              |
| `campObject`           | `Camp`                     |                                                              |
| `clubObject`           | `Club`                     |                                                              |
| `dropdownOptionsArray` | `CustomFieldOption[]`, optional | present for `select` and `radio`                        |
| `cloned_from`          | `CustomField`, optional    | self-referential; points at the row this was cloned from     |

It carries `archived`, so extend `ArchiveAttributes` (see `types.ts:4-6`) rather than redeclaring it. `CustomField` is declared before `Camp` and `CampClass` in the file — TypeScript interfaces hoist, so a forward reference is fine; only move a declaration if the compiler actually objects.

**2. Add a `CustomFieldOption` class** for `dropdownOptionsArray` to deserialize into. Its attributes have NOT been reverse-engineered. Register it bare, exactly like the existing unexplored classes at `types.ts:48-64` (`StripeAccount`, `Profile`, `EntryFee`) — those sit under a comment at `:44-46` explaining why they exist. Its `objectClass` is `customFieldOptions`. Add it to that existing group rather than inventing a new pattern.

**3. `CustomFieldResponse` (`types.ts:353-356`)** is missing a field:
- `optionObjectID?: string` — present for `select` and `radio` answers, pointing at the chosen `customFieldOptions` row.

**4. `ParticipantAttributes` (`types.ts:358-403`)** is missing these real fields. All are optional:

- `weight?: string` — a numeric string (`"105"`). Populated on 118 of 168. Type it as the string Clubspot actually returns; converting is the sync's job, not the SDK's.
- `pcpName?: string`, `pcpNumber?: string` — primary care physician, matching `Camp.collect_pcp`.
- `emergencyEmail?: string`
- `emergencyContact_secondary?: string`, `emergencyMobile_secondary?: string`, `emergencyRelationship_secondary?: string`, `emergencyEmail_secondary?: string` — a complete second emergency contact, mirroring the existing primary set at `types.ts:373-375` and the secondary guardian set at `:381-383`.
- `crewPosition?: string`
- `ticket?: unknown` — always present on event participants; shape not reverse-engineered.
- `primary?: boolean`

Note `types.ts:390-392` currently says `contactsArray`/`members`/`members_external` are "always observed empty in CSC data so far". That still holds; leave it.

## Scope fence

- `packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts` only. Do not touch `queries.ts`, `main.ts`, `parse.ts`, `functions.ts`, or any other package.
- Do NOT add CLI subcommands. The `@register` decorator already gives every registered class generic `get`/`list` subcommands via the `schemas` list (`parse.ts:20`, `main.ts:110`) — registering `CustomFieldOption` is enough.
- Do NOT change `packages/crm/schema.yaml` or the design doc.
- Do NOT act on any of these fields — no mapping, no sync code. Steps 3 and 5-9 do that.
- Do not widen `clubspot-sdk`'s `engines.node` bound, tempting as it is; #53 tracks that separately.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- `CustomField` has typed attributes and `Camp.customFieldsArray` (`types.ts:224`) still type-checks against it.
- A test is not required — this is a type declaration change with no logic. Do not invent one to satisfy a convention; if `tsc` accepts the file and the existing 82 tests still pass, the change is verified.

Commit once.

### Authentication to Directus

The job authenticates with a Directus static token held by a machine user.

1. `randomSecret("clubspot-sync-directus-token")` in `directus.ts` generates the value and stores
   it in Secret Manager.
2. `DirectusUser` gains an optional `token` input. It provisions OIDC users only today — `provider`
   and `external_identifier`, no password and no token
   (`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus.ts:362-376`). The provider passes `token`
   through on create and update. The machine user uses `provider: "default"` and no external
   identifier.
3. Pulumi passes the generated value straight into the resource. No read back from Secret Manager
   is needed. Reading a secret value at apply time is precedented (`people-hub.ts:42`), but this
   case avoids it.
4. The Cloud Run job reads the secret through `secretKeyRef`, the same shape as
   `run-reports-job.ts:80`. The job's service account gets `secret.grant(...)`.

A new `DirectusRole` "Clubspot Sync" holds least privilege at the Directus layer: `appAccess:
false`, create and read and update on the collections it writes, create on `sync_runs` and
`sync_program_runs`, and no delete anywhere. The sync never deletes a row. It sets
`status = cancelled`. The role needs no permission filters, so it needs no Directus license

input.prompt:
Step 3 of the approved design doc at `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`. Add `just directus-local`: tooling that stands up Directus and Postgres as local containers and applies `packages/crm/schema.yaml` to them. Steps 4 through 10 test against this and step 12 verifies with it, so it is a committed tool, not a throwaway.

## Task

**A compose file plus a script**, following the repo's existing conventions:

- `just` recipes are one-liners that delegate to `scripts/<name>` — see `justfile` and the `scripts/` directory (`scripts/doctor`, `scripts/db-tunnel`, `scripts/deploy` are the models). Recipes carry a `#` doc comment; the recipe belongs in the `[dev]` group.
- `scripts/*` are `bash` with `set -euo pipefail` and `cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."`. `scripts/worktree` is a short, clear example.

**Pin the versions to production.** Directus must be `directus/directus:12.3.1`, matching `packages/substrate/deploy/docker-compose.yml:60` — a snapshot regenerated against a different Directus version produces a snapshot whose recorded version does not match the pinned image, which is exactly the bug #101 was filed for. Use a Postgres version matching the Cloud SQL instance; check `packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/database.ts` for the configured version and match its major.

input.command:
gh issue create --title "Schema apply verification misses dropped relation metadata" --label "bug,P2" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

`applySchema` verifies a schema apply by checking that every collection the app owns exists
afterward (`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus-client.ts:226-234`). That check was
added because a `204` from `/schema/apply` doesn't prove anything persisted — see the comment at
`:222`. But it only looks at collections. Relations, and the Postgres foreign-key constraints they
carry, are not checked.

`scripts/directus-local` has the same gap: its retry loop compares expected collections against
`GET /collections` and stops there.

This surfaced while applying the schema changes for #70. Adding the reverse aliases on `people` via
`PATCH /relations/<collection>/<field>` with only a `meta` block caused Directus to treat the
omitted `schema` block as "no schema" and silently drop the foreign-key constraints
`contacts_person_id_foreign` and `registrations_person_id_foreign`, including their
`ON DELETE CASCADE`. Both checks reported success. It was caught by a round-trip snapshot diff and
confirmed with `psql \d`, then fixed by recreating the relations with `POST /relations` and a full
schema block.

The committed schema is correct — all 23 relations carry a `constraint_name` and an `on_delete`.
The gap is that nothing would have told us if they didn't.

## Fix

Extend the post-apply verification to cover relations, not just collections: compare the submitted
snapshot's `relations[]` against the live snapshot, checking `constraint_name` and `on_delete`
survived. `getSnapshot` already returns relations (`directus-client.ts:105-112`), so the data is in
hand.

Mirror the same check in `scripts/directus-local`'s retry loop.

Add a regression test alongside the existing `fetch`-stubbed cases in
`packages/infrastructure/test/directus-client.test.ts`: an apply whose live snapshot comes back with
a relation missing its constraint should throw rather than report success.

## Impact

A silently dropped FK constraint is a data-integrity hole that no current check would catch. The
risky operation here was a hand-issued `PATCH /relations`, which `applySchema` itself doesn't do —
it submits a full diff — so this is latent rather than active. But schema changes are applied to
production by `pulumi up`, and "the apply said it worked" is currently a weaker guarantee than it
looks.
EOF
)"

content.text:
**Step 4 landed** (`43ccead7`) — and it caught a real bug worth telling you about.

Adding the reverse aliases on `people` via `PATCH /relations` with only a `meta` block made Directus treat the omitted `schema` block as "no schema" and **silently drop the foreign-key constraints** on `contacts.person_id` and `registrations.person_id`, `ON DELETE CASCADE` included. Both the schema-apply check and the local tool's retry loop reported success. It was caught by a round-trip diff, confirmed against `psql \d`, and fixed by recreating the relations with `POST /relations` and a full schema block.

I verified that independently rather than taking it on faith: all 23 relations in the committed snapshot carry a `constraint_name` and an `on_delete`, and both repaired relations are correct — `contact_links` and `registration_links` with `ON DELETE CASCADE` intact.

**Filed #126** for the underlying gap, because it outlives this session: post-apply verification checks that collections exist but never checks relations, so a dropped FK constraint is invisible to both `applySchema` and `scripts/directus-local`. The risky operation was hand-issued, and `applySchema` submits a full diff instead, so it's latent rather than active — but "the apply said it worked" is currently a weaker guarantee than it looks, and schema changes reach production through `pulumi up`.

The schema now carries `registration_billing`, `custom_field_definitions`, `custom_field_responses`, `sync_runs`, and `sync_program_runs`, plus the new fields and `is_unique: true` on every `clubspot_*_id`. `docs/crm-schema.md` was rewritten to match — billing is no longer described as out of scope, person identity is documented as resolved, and the stale "open questions for #95" section is gone.

**Seven judgment calls it made and flagged**, all of which I think are right. The one worth your eye: `sync_program_runs.clubspot_camp_id` is deliberately **excluded** from the blanket `is_unique: true` rule — many log rows reference the same camp across runs, so uniqueness would break the append-only log. Also, the twelve billing cent fields are not-nullable defaulting to `0` rather than nullable, for clean arithmetic.

I'm re-running the clean-teardown → apply → re-apply idempotence check in the background to confirm the snapshot is self-consistent. That's the criterion that actually matters, and I'd rather verify it myself than inherit it. I'll report when it finishes, then move to step 6.

input.description: Add camp discovery and sync log
input.prompt:
Step 6 of the approved design doc at `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`. In `packages/clubspot-sync`, add camp discovery, change detection with its refresh floor, and the sync log with per-camp watermarks. Unit tests included.

Read the doc's "What the job syncs, and when" (around line 100) and "The sync log" (around line 130) sections — they are the specification.

No mapping code and no CLI in this step. This builds the layer that decides *which* camps to sync and records *what happened*. Steps 7 through 9 add the mappings; step 10 adds the CLI.

## What already exists

- `packages/clubspot-sync/src/directus.ts` — `DirectusClient` with `readItems`, `createItems`, `updateItem`, a `dryRun` constructor flag, and Directus filter encoding (`_eq`, `_icontains`). Tests at `packages/clubspot-sync/test/directus.test.ts` show the `fetch`-stubbing pattern.
- `@cyc-seattle/clubspot-sdk` is already a declared dependency. `LoggedQuery` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/parse.ts`) is the query wrapper the reports use; `Camp`, `CampSession`, `CampClass`, `Registration`, `RegistrationCampSession` are in `types.ts`.
- The `sync_runs` and `sync_program_runs` collections exist in `packages/crm/schema.yaml` as of last commit. Their applied fields are exactly:
  - `sync_runs` — `id`, `started_at`, `finished_at` (nullable), `status`, `programs_checked`, `programs_synced`, `error` (nullable)
  - `sync_program_runs` — `id`, `run_id`, `program_id` (nullable), `clubspot_camp_id`, `started_at`, `finished_at` (nullable), `status`, `items_created`, `items_updated`, `error` (nullable)
- A local Directus is running right now with this schema applied, if you want to check a query by hand. `just directus-local` / `just directus-local-down` manage it.

## Task

**Camp discovery.** List every non-archived `Camp` for a club. `packages/admin-functions/src/camps.ts:37` already does exactly this query — match it.

**Change detection.** A camp's own `updatedAt` does not move when a child object changes, so per camp issue one `Parse.Query.count()` per child class filtered on `updatedAt >= watermark`: `CampSession`, `CampClass`, `Registration`, `RegistrationCampSession`. If every count is zero *and* the camp's own `updatedAt` predates the watermark, skip the camp.

Note `EntryCap` has no pointer to a camp (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts`, `EntryCapAttributes`), so a capacity-only change is invisible to these counts, and nothing in `updatedAt` reveals a delete. Both holes are closed by the same rule: **a camp whose last successful sync is more than 24 hours old is synced regardless of the counts.** That is a refresh floor, not a snooze — the doc argues explicitly against building a snooze now, so don't.

**Per-camp watermark.** The watermark for a camp is the greatest `started_at` among its `sync_program_runs` rows with `status = ok`, or the epoch if there are none. It is deliberately **per camp, not per run** — if camp A succeeds and camp B fails in the same run, a run-level watermark would advance past B's missed window. Use the run's `started_at`, not `finished_at`, so a Clubspot write made during the run is picked up next time.

**The log.** One `sync_runs` row per job execution, created at start with `status = running` and updated at the end. One `sync_program_runs` row per camp the run touched, with `status` of `ok`, `failed`, or `skipped`. `program_id` is nullable because the first sync of a camp has no `programs` row yet.

## Shape

Follow the doc's "Shape of the sync" section and `packages/admin-functions/src/roster.ts`: a **pure function decides**, a thin executor acts. Specifically, the decision "which of these camps need syncing, given these watermarks and this clock" must be a pure function over plain data — camp id, camp `updatedAt`, the four counts, the watermark, and `now`. That function is where the refresh floor and the skip rule live, and it is what the tests exercise. Keep Parse queries and Directus writes out of it.

That matters because the alternative — testing this through mocked Parse queries and a stubbed `fetch` — makes the interesting logic (the 24-hour floor, the epoch fallback, the "counts are zero but the camp itself changed" case) expensive to cover.

## Tests

`packages/clubspot-sync/test/`, following `packages/clubspot-sync/test/directus.test.ts` and `packages/admin-functions/test/roster.test.ts` (which builds fake Parse objects with an `id` and a `get`). Cover at minimum:

- A camp with all-zero counts and a recent watermark is skipped.
- A camp with a non-zero count on any one of the four child classes is synced.
- A camp with zero counts whose own `updatedAt` is newer than the watermark is synced.
- The 24-hour refresh floor forces a sync despite zero counts and a fresh-looking camp.
- A camp with no prior successful run uses the epoch, so it always syncs.
- Watermark selection picks the greatest `started_at` among `ok` rows only, ignoring `failed` and `skipped` rows.
- Time is injected, not read from the system clock, so the floor is testable without sleeping.

## Scope fence

- New files under `packages/clubspot-sync/src/` and `test/` only.
- Do NOT add a `main.ts` or any CLI wiring — step 10.
- Do NOT write mapping code for `programs`, `sessions`, `classes`, `people`, `registrations`, or any other CRM collection — steps 7 through 9. This step's output is "here are the camps to sync" plus the log rows; it does not sync anything.
- Do NOT modify `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `docs/crm-schema.md`, `scripts/directus-local`, or the justfile.
- Do NOT modify `packages/clubspot-sdk` or `packages/admin-functions`.
- Do NOT add npm dependencies beyond what the package already declares.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- The decision logic is a pure function with direct unit tests, not reachable only through mocks.
- No system-clock reads in the decision path.

Commit once.

input.prompt:
Step 7 of the approved design doc at `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`. In `packages/clubspot-sync`, add the schedule mapping and reconcile plan: `programs`, `sessions`, `classes`, `session_classes`, `entry_caps`. Unit tests included.

Read the doc's "Shape of the sync" section (around line 76). The schedule pass is a **full reconcile per camp, not watermark-filtered** — a class, session, or cap can change without the camp's `updatedAt` moving, and `packages/admin-functions/src/sessions.ts:56` already takes this approach for the same reason.

## What already exists

- `packages/clubspot-sync/src/directus.ts` — `DirectusClient` (`readItems`, `createItems`, `updateItem`, `dryRun` flag).
- `packages/clubspot-sync/src/change-detection.ts` — `needsSync`, a pure decision function. Follow its shape: a pure function over plain data, tested directly, with the Parse/Directus I/O in a thin separate executor.
- `packages/clubspot-sync/src/camps.ts`, `src/sync-log.ts`.
- A local Directus with the current schema is running (`just directus-local` / `just directus-local-down`) if you want to check a query by hand.

## The mapping

Clubspot → CRM, with the dedup key in each case being the `clubspot_*_id` column, which is now `is_unique: true` in `packages/crm/schema.yaml`:

| CRM collection    | Clubspot source | Key                        |
| ----------------- | --------------- | -------------------------- |
| `programs`        | `Camp`          | `clubspot_camp_id`         |
| `sessions`        | `CampSession`   | `clubspot_session_id`      |
| `classes`         | `CampClass`     | `clubspot_class_id`        |
| `entry_caps`      | `EntryCap`      | `clubspot_entry_cap_id`    |
| `session_classes` | derived         | none — see below           |

Field-level notes the doc settles:

- `sessions.name` ← `CampSession.name`. This column was only added last commit; it did not exist before.
- `programs.category` stays null — `CampAttributes` has no category field.
- `entry_caps.session_id` is nullable, and null means the cap applies to that class across every session. That is Clubspot's own shape (`EntryCapAttributes.campSessionObject` is optional).
- `classes.program_id` — a class belongs to the program, independent of which sessions offer it.

**`session_classes` is the one that needs real logic.** Clubspot represents a session's classes as either an explicit `CampSession.campClassesArray` or an `allClasses` flag meaning "every class in the program". The sync **expands the `allClasses` case into one row per program class at sync time**, so the table always holds the explicit list and nothing downstream special-cases the flag. It has no Clubspot id of its own, so reconcile it to match Clubspot's current state each run: add rows that appeared, remove rows that no longer exist.

`packages/admin-functions/src/sessions.ts:74-76` shows the existing `allClasses` handling (`campSession.get("campClassesArray") ?? allClasses`) and `:90-98` shows the matching entry-cap rule, including that a cap with no session belongs to a session marked `allClasses`. Read both — they encode real behavior learned from production data.

## Shape

A **pure plan function** per collection, plus a thin executor. The plan function takes the Clubspot objects and the existing CRM rows, and returns what to create and what to update — the same "read everything once, key by `clubspot_*_id`, diff" approach the doc describes. Parse objects reaching the plan function are fine (the tests fake them with `id` and `get`, as `packages/admin-functions/test/roster.test.ts` does), but no queries and no writes inside it.

`session_classes` additionally returns rows to **remove**, since it is the only collection here that reconciles by deletion rather than by key. Note the design doc says the sync never deletes CRM rows elsewhere — `session_classes` is the stated exception because it is a pure join with no Clubspot identity. Removing a `session_classes` row is not destroying data; it is unlinking a class from a session that no longer offers it.

Dependency order matters on create: `programs` before `sessions` and `classes`, both before `session_classes` and `entry_caps`, because the child rows carry FKs to rows that may not exist yet on a first sync. Make that ordering explicit rather than incidental.

## Tests

`packages/clubspot-sync/test/`, following the existing tests there. Cover at minimum:

- A camp not yet in the CRM produces a create; one already present with the same values produces neither a create nor an update.
- A changed field on an existing row produces an update keyed on the existing CRM row's id.
- `allClasses: true` expands to one `session_classes` row per class in the program.
- An explicit `campClassesArray` produces exactly those rows and no others.
- A `session_classes` row whose class is no longer offered by that session is removed.
- An entry cap with no session applies across sessions; one with a session does not.
- Create ordering puts `programs` before its dependents.

## Scope fence

- New files under `packages/clubspot-sync/src/` and `test/` only.
- Do NOT map `people`, `contacts`, `medical_profiles`, `registrations`, `registration_entries`, `registration_billing`, or `custom_field_*` — steps 8 and 9.
- Do NOT add a `main.ts` or CLI wiring — step 10.
- Do NOT modify `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `docs/crm-schema.md`, `scripts/directus-local`, or the justfile.
- Do NOT modify `packages/clubspot-sdk` or `packages/admin-functions`.
- If a field you need is missing from the schema, stop and report it rather than adding it — a schema change now means regenerating the snapshot, which is a whole step.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- The plan functions are pure and directly unit-tested, not reachable only through mocks.
- No Directus write happens for a row whose values are unchanged.

Commit once.

input.prompt:
Step 8 of the approved design doc at `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`. In `packages/clubspot-sync`, add person matching and the person mapping: `people`, `contacts`, `medical_profiles`. Unit tests included.

**Read the doc's "Person identity" section (around line 168) in full before writing anything.** It is the specification and it was revised twice after review — the design it describes is not the obvious one.

This is the subtlest step in the plan. The rules below are deliberate, not incidental.

## The one rule that matters most

**A person reference is resolved once, when the row that points at it is created, and never re-resolved.** `contacts.person_id` and `registrations.person_id` point at `people`. On every later run the sync leaves an existing row's `person_id` exactly as it is.

That is the entire reason a manual merge survives. Staff repoint the FK, delete the loser, and no later sync undoes it. A design that re-derives the match each run would silently revert every merge a human ever made. If you find yourself writing code that recomputes `person_id` for an existing row, stop — that is the bug this design exists to prevent.

## Matching at creation

Directus REST filters give `_eq` and `_icontains` and nothing else — no trigram, no similarity operator. So "fuzzy" means: normalize, fetch a small candidate set with an indexable filter, and compare in the client.

1. **Normalize** — trim, lowercase, collapse inner whitespace, strip punctuation from names. Phone numbers to digits only.
2. **Fetch candidates** — with an email, `filter[email][_eq]`. Without one, `filter[last_name][_icontains]` with a bounded limit.
3. **Match in the client, by kind:**
   - **Participant** — same normalized first and last name, and the same `date_of_birth`. If there is no date of birth, additionally require the same normalized email.
   - **Guardian** — same normalized email and same normalized last name. Allow an edit distance of one on the first name: that catches a typo but must not match "Bob" against "Robert".
   - **Emergency contact** — same normalized full name and same normalized phone. Match on `emergencyEmail` when present, but it is filled on roughly 1 in 168 real participants, so name plus phone is the working path.
4. **No match creates a new `people` row.**

**The matcher is deliberately reluctant.** A false split makes a duplicate that staff merge in a minute. A false merge silently attaches one family's registration to another person's record, and the data it corrupts is medical and emergency data. When in doubt, create. Encode that bias; do not "improve" the matcher to catch more matches.

**An email alone is never a match.** Families share one address, so `parentGuardianEmail` and `parentGuardianEmail_secondary` are frequently the same string for two different adults.

**Updating an existing person fills gaps only.** If `people.email` is null and the registration supplies one, write it. If it already holds a value, leave it. That keeps a staff edit — and a merge — from being overwritten by the next registration naming the same person.

## The mapping

Source is a Clubspot `Participant` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts`). Note the SDK's `ParticipantAttributes` was corrected two commits ago; several fields below only exist as of that change.

**people** — `first_name` (not null), `last_name` (nullable), `email`, `phone`, `date_of_birth`, `gender`, `street`, `city`, `state`, `postal_code`.
- `gender` ← `Participant.gender`. Verified populated on 168/168 real camp participants.
- `postal_code` ← `Participant.zip`.
- A free-text contact name splits on the first space: first token to `first_name`, the rest to `last_name`. A single token goes to `last_name`, leaving `first_name`... — `first_name` is NOT nullable in the schema, so decide what a single-token name does and make it consistent. Report the call you made.

**contacts** — `related_person_id` (the minor), `person_id` (the guardian or emergency contact), `relationship_type` (`guardian` | `emergency_contact`), `contact_order`, `relationship_detail`.
- Guardians come from `parentGuardianName`/`Email`/`Mobile` and the `_secondary` set; `contact_order` recovers primary vs secondary.
- Emergency contacts come from `emergencyContact`/`emergencyMobile`/`emergencyRelationship`/`emergencyEmail`, **and a full secondary set exists too** (`emergencyContact_secondary`, `emergencyMobile_secondary`, `emergencyRelationship_secondary`, `emergencyEmail_secondary`). Both map the same way, distinguished by `contact_order`.
- `relationship_detail` ← `emergencyRelationship` ("Aunt").

**medical_profiles** — one row per person, `person_id` unique.
- `conditions` ← `medical`, `allergies` ← `medical_allergies`, `medications` ← `medical_meds`, `last_tetanus` ← `medical_tetanus`.
- `physician_name` ← `pcpName`, `physician_phone` ← `pcpNumber`. Both real fields; CYC has used them on 1 of 168, so expect null.
- `weight` ← `Participant.weight`, which Clubspot sends as a numeric **string**. Parse to integer. **Drop a value that does not parse rather than storing junk** — at least one real row holds `"1"`, so a plausibility floor is reasonable if you want one, but do not silently coerce garbage.

## Shape

Follow `packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts` exactly: pure plan functions plus a thin executor, with `planByKey`/`diffFields` style helpers where they fit.

The wrinkle here is that matching needs a candidate fetch, so it cannot be wholly pure. Split it so the **decision** is pure — given a normalized candidate set and a normalized input, which candidate matches, if any — and the fetching is a thin executor around it. That decision function is what the tests exercise.

## Tests

Cover at minimum:
- Each of the three match rules, positive and negative.
- Edit distance one matches a guardian first-name typo; "Bob" vs "Robert" does not match.
- Two different guardians sharing one family email are NOT merged.
- A participant with no date of birth requires an email to match.
- Fill-gaps-only: an existing non-null field is never overwritten; a null one is filled.
- An existing `contacts` row keeps its `person_id` across a re-sync even when the matcher would now choose differently. **This is the regression test for the merge-durability rule — make sure it exists.**
- Name splitting, including the single-token case.
- `weight` parses, and an unparseable value is dropped rather than written.
- Primary and secondary guardians and emergency contacts get distinct `contact_order`.

## Scope fence

- New files under `packages/clubspot-sync/src/` and `test/` only.
- Do NOT map `registrations`, `registration_entries`, `registration_billing`, or `custom_field_*` — step 9. You may define how a registration *supplies* a participant, but do not write registration rows.
- Do NOT add a `main.ts` or CLI wiring — step 10.
- Do NOT modify `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `docs/crm-schema.md`, `scripts/directus-local`, or the justfile. If a field is missing, stop and report rather than adding it.
- Do NOT modify `packages/clubspot-sdk` or `packages/admin-functions`.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- The match decision is a pure function with direct unit tests.
- The merge-durability regression test exists and passes.
- No code path recomputes `person_id` for an existing row.

Report the single-token name call and anything else you had to decide rather than copy.

Commit once.

```
registrations            id, person_id, program_id, clubspot_registration_id,
                         registered_at (not null), status (not null),
                         waiver_status (nullable), archived (not null),
                         clubspot_participant_id
registration_entries     id, registration_id, session_id, class_id,
                         status (not null), clubspot_session_join_id
registration_billing     id, registration_id, amount, amount_pending, amount_received,
                         amount_refunded, amount_capturable, amount_deferred,
                         deferred_amount_billed, discount, processing_fee,
                         processing_passed_on, application_fee_amount, tax,
                         currency, clubspot_billing_id
                         (every money field is NOT NULL, default 0)
custom_field_definitions id, program_id, label, field_type, required,
                         clubspot_custom_field_id
custom_field_responses   id, registration_id, definition_id, value
```

## The mapping

**registrations** ← Clubspot `Registration`.
- `person_id` comes from `PersonSync.syncParticipant` on the registration's participant. Clubspot now allows only one participant per registration, though `participantsArray` is still an array — handle an empty array without crashing.
- `clubspot_participant_id` is that participant's id. It lives here, not on `people`, because a Clubspot participant id is per registration, not per human.
- `registered_at` ← `confirmed_at`. It is NOT NULL in the schema, so decide what an unconfirmed registration does and report the call. Note `queryCampEntries` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/queries.ts:9`) filters to `.exists("confirmed_at")`, which is worth knowing before you invent a fallback.
- `status` ← `Registration.status`, `waiver_status` ← `waiver_status`, `archived` ← `archived ?? false`.

**registration_entries** ← `RegistrationCampSession` (the "Session Join Id" in the old report), keyed on `clubspot_session_join_id`.
- `status` folds Clubspot's precedence: **archived wins, then waitlist, then the registration's own status**. `packages/admin-functions/src/participants.ts:87-100` (`calculateStatus`) is the existing implementation of exactly this rule — read it.
- **Vanished entries.** When a session is removed from a registration, Clubspot drops the join object entirely, so it cannot be detected by looking at what Clubspot returns. The old code worked around this by marking every row for the participant `cancelled` first and then rewriting the survivors (`participants.ts:111-130`). Do NOT reproduce that. Instead: fetch the existing `registration_entries` for that registration and set `status = cancelled` on any whose `clubspot_session_join_id` is no longer present in Clubspot's current set. No global pre-pass, and no deletes — the sync never deletes a row here, it cancels.

**registration_billing** ← `BillingRegistration` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:120-139`), one row per registration.
- **Amounts are integer cents, stored exactly as Clubspot holds them.** `packages/admin-functions/src/registrations.ts:26-32` divides by 100 for display, which confirms the source unit. Do not convert on write.
- Every money column is NOT NULL with a default of 0, and several of Clubspot's own fields are optional — so a missing value becomes 0, not null.
- `cartObject`, `customer`, and `stripeAccount` are not modeled. They are Stripe plumbing.
- A registration with no `billing_registration` gets no row; don't fabricate a zeroed one.

**custom_field_definitions** ← the camp's `customFieldsArray` (`CustomField` objects), keyed on `clubspot_custom_field_id`.
- `label` ← `CustomField.name`. **Not `label`** — and it can run to thousands of characters, which is why the column is `text`.
- `field_type` ← `CustomField.type` (`text`, `select`, `radio`, `file_upload`).
- Definitions are per camp, so `program_id` is the camp's program. The same logical question exists as a separate row per camp; that is expected and is not something to deduplicate.

**custom_field_responses** ← the participant's `customFieldsArray` (`CustomFieldResponse`: `{ customFieldID, response, optionObjectID? }`).
- `definition_id` resolves via `customFieldID` → the `custom_field_definitions` row with that `clubspot_custom_field_id`.
- `value` ← `response`. `optionObjectID` is not modeled; `response` already holds the chosen option's text.
- A response whose `customFieldID` matches no known definition should be skipped rather than crash the run — definitions can be archived or belong to another camp.

## Shape

Pure plan functions plus a thin executor, as in `schedule.ts`. Ordering on create: `registrations` before `registration_entries`, `registration_billing`, and `custom_field_responses`, all of which carry a FK to it. `custom_field_definitions` before `custom_field_responses`.

## Tests

Cover at minimum:
- A new registration creates a row; an unchanged one produces no write.
- `calculateStatus` precedence: archived beats waitlist beats the registration's status, all three.
- An entry present in the CRM but absent from Clubspot's current set is set to `cancelled` — and one still present is not.
- Cancelling a vanished entry does not touch other registrations' entries.
- Billing maps cents through unchanged, and a missing optional amount becomes 0.
- A registration with no billing object produces no `registration_billing` row.
- A custom field response resolves to its definition; one with an unknown `customFieldID` is skipped.
- `label` comes from `CustomField.name`.

## Scope fence

- New files under `packages/clubspot-sync/src/` and `test/` only.
- Do NOT add a `main.ts` or CLI wiring, and do NOT write the top-level run loop that ties the passes together — step 10.
- Do NOT modify `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `docs/crm-schema.md`, `scripts/directus-local`, or the justfile. If a field is missing, stop and report it.
- Do NOT modify `packages/clubspot-sdk`, `packages/admin-functions`, or the existing `people.ts` / `person-sync.ts` / `schedule.ts` beyond what is needed to import from them. If one of them needs a change, say so rather than reshaping it.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- The plan functions are pure and directly unit-tested.
- No Directus write for an unchanged row.
- No code path deletes a `registration_entries` row.

Report the `registered_at` call and anything else you decided rather than copied.

Commit once.

content.text:
Step 9 running — registrations, entries, billing, and custom fields.

Two things I pointed it at specifically:

**The vanished-entry problem.** When a session is removed from a registration, Clubspot deletes the join object outright, so there's nothing in the response to react to. The old report worked around it by marking *every* row for that participant `cancelled` and then rewriting the survivors — a global pre-pass with a self-deprecating comment above it (`participants.ts:111`). I told it explicitly not to reproduce that: fetch the existing entries for that one registration, cancel the ones whose join id is gone. And cancel, never delete.

**`calculateStatus` precedence** — archived beats waitlist beats the registration's own status. That already exists at `participants.ts:87-100` and encodes real behavior, so it gets read rather than reinvented.

I also flagged `registered_at` as a decision it has to make and report: the column is NOT NULL, but `confirmed_at` is optional on an unconfirmed registration. Worth knowing that `queryCampEntries` already filters to `.exists("confirmed_at")`, so the case may not arise in practice — but inventing a silent fallback would be the wrong instinct.

Here are the steps.

## The DWD lookup for #58

**What it's for:** before deleting `admin-scripts-runner@`, you need to know whether its client ID has domain-wide delegation authorized in Workspace. DWD lives in the Admin console, not in GCP IAM — so a clean `gcloud` audit showing no project bindings still won't tell you. Delete an SA that holds a DWD grant and you silently break whatever was impersonating a Workspace admin through it.

**Step 1 — confirm whose client ID that is.** `115185692211855827749` isn't in the repo; the two recorded there are `substrate-runner` (115457003008765084595) and `report-runner` (116667448905851774279). So it's presumably the legacy SA, but confirm rather than assume:

```
gcloud iam service-accounts list --project=cyc-admin-scripts \
  --format="table(email,uniqueId,disabled)"
```

The `uniqueId` column *is* the DWD client ID. If `115185692211855827749` doesn't match `admin-scripts-runner@`, stop — you're about to audit the wrong account.

**Step 2 — look it up in the Admin console.** As a super-admin: **Workspace Admin → Security → Access and data control → API controls → Domain-wide delegation**. That page lists authorized client IDs with their scopes. Search for `115185692211855827749`.

- **Not listed** → no DWD. Deleting the SA can't break a Workspace integration, and #58 comes down to the ordinary IAM audit already in its scope.
- **Listed** → record the exact scopes in the issue before touching anything. Those scopes are the evidence for what was using it, and they're the thing that disappears irreversibly on delete.

**Step 3 — the real caution.** A DWD grant is keyed to the numeric client ID, and that ID is *not* reused if you recreate an SA with the same name. `.claude/plans/deployer-access.md:180` records exactly this: deleting and recreating either live SA is unsafe because it breaks DWD. So if this one is listed, deleting it is a one-way door — revoke the delegation entry deliberately as its own step rather than as a side effect.

Worth noting §5.2 is the working example of a grant that matters: `substrate-runner`'s client ID is authorized for `admin.directory.group.readonly`, which is what lets oauth2-proxy read group membership for the portal. That's the shape of thing you're checking for.

input.description: Add clubspot-sync CLI and run loop
input.prompt:
Step 10 of the approved design doc at `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`. Add the CLI and the run loop to `packages/clubspot-sync`: `--dry-run`, `--camp <id>`, and the orchestration that ties the existing pieces together.

Read the doc's "What the job syncs, and when" (around line 100) and "Verification" sections.

## What already exists — wire these up, don't rewrite them

- `src/camps.ts` — `discoverCamps(clubId)`.
- `src/change-detection.ts` — `countChildChanges(camp, watermark)` (Parse executor) and `needsSync(input)` (pure), plus `REFRESH_FLOOR_MS`.
- `src/sync-log.ts` — `SyncLog` (`startRun`, `finishRun`, `recordProgramRun`, `priorProgramRuns`) and `watermarkForCamp(rows, campId)`.
- `src/schedule.ts` — `planPrograms`, `planClasses`, `planSessions`, `planEntryCaps`, `planSessionClasses`, `SCHEDULE_CREATE_ORDER`, and the shared `planByKey` / `diffFields` / `requireLookup` helpers.
- `src/people.ts` + `src/person-sync.ts` — `PersonSync.syncParticipant(participant)` returns `{ id, created }`.
- `src/registrations.ts` — `planRegistrations`, the entry/billing/custom-field plans, `REGISTRATION_CREATE_ORDER`.
- `src/directus.ts` — `DirectusClient(baseUrl, token, dryRun)`.

Everything needed already exists as tested units. This step is composition plus a CLI.

## The CLI

`src/main.ts`, following `packages/admin-functions/src/main.ts` closely — it is the working model for this repo's CLI shape: `@commander-js/extra-typings`, a `preAction` hook that configures winston and initializes Clubspot, `LoggingOption` / `VerboseOption` from `@cyc-seattle/commodore`, and `ClubspotUsernameOption` / `ClubspotPasswordOption` from `@cyc-seattle/clubspot-sdk`. Add a `bin` entry to `package.json` as the other CLI packages do.

Options:
- `--club <id>`, env `CLUBSPOT_CLUB_ID`, mandatory. The doc settles that the job syncs one club and takes the id from the environment.
- `--directus-url <url>`, env `DIRECTUS_URL`, mandatory.
- `--directus-token <token>`, env `DIRECTUS_TOKEN`, mandatory. Prefer the env var — CLAUDE.md and #49 both record that a secret passed as a flag is visible in `ps`, so do not encourage the flag in help text.
- `--dry-run` — logs planned writes, performs none. `DirectusClient` already implements this; thread the flag through.
- `--camp <id>` — sync only this camp, bypassing discovery and change detection. This is what the doc's verification plan uses for the first real run against one finished camp.

## The run loop

1. Open a `sync_runs` row (`status = running`).
2. Discover the club's camps, or use just `--camp` when given.
3. Read the prior `sync_program_runs` once, so each camp's watermark comes from memory rather than a query per camp.
4. Per camp: compute the watermark, count child changes, and call `needsSync`. Skip means a `sync_program_runs` row with `status = skipped` and nothing else.
5. For a camp that needs syncing, run the schedule pass then the registration pass, respecting `SCHEDULE_CREATE_ORDER` and `REGISTRATION_CREATE_ORDER`. The registration pass needs `PersonSync` to resolve each registration's participant first, since `registrations.person_id` is NOT NULL.
6. Record one `sync_program_runs` row per camp with counts and status.
7. Close the `sync_runs` row.

**A camp that fails must not abort the run.** Catch per camp, record `status = failed` with the error, and continue to the next one. That is the whole reason the watermark is per camp rather than per run — one camp failing must not advance another's window, and must not cost the run. Exit non-zero if any camp failed, so Cloud Run marks the execution failed.

**Log errors explicitly.** `packages/admin-functions/src/runner.ts:129-134` documents why: `Error.message` and `.stack` are non-enumerable, so an error object serializes to `{}` under the JSON logging format unless you pull them out by hand.

Which Clubspot queries feed the passes is yours to choose, but `packages/clubspot-sdk/src/queries.ts`'s `queryCampEntries` (`:9`) is the existing query for a camp's registrations and already includes `sessionJoinObjects.campSessionObject`, `sessionJoinObjects.campClassObject`, and `participantsArray`. Note it filters to `.exists("confirmed_at")`, which is what makes `buildRegistrationRow`'s throw-on-missing-`confirmed_at` safe.

## Tests

The plan functions are already covered. Test what this step adds:
- A camp that `needsSync` rejects produces a `skipped` log row and no collection writes.
- One camp throwing does not prevent a later camp from syncing, and the run still closes.
- A run where a camp failed exits non-zero.
- `--dry-run` performs no writes — including no `sync_runs` or `sync_program_runs` writes, or if you decide the log should still be written in a dry run, test and justify whichever you choose.

Stub `fetch` as the existing tests do; fake Parse objects with `id` and `get` per `packages/admin-functions/test/roster.test.ts`.

## Scope fence

- `packages/clubspot-sync` only, plus its `package.json`.
- Do NOT modify the existing plan functions in `schedule.ts`, `registrations.ts`, `people.ts`, `person-sync.ts`, `camps.ts`, `change-detection.ts`, or `sync-log.ts`. If one genuinely needs a change to be composable, make the smallest possible one and say so in your report.
- Do NOT add Pulumi resources, a Dockerfile target, a Cloud Run job, or a service account — step 11.
- Do NOT modify `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, or the justfile.
- Do NOT add Google Chat notifications. The sync writes failures to the log and exits non-zero; notifications are deferred to #122.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- `node packages/clubspot-sync/dist/main.js --help` lists the options.
- A camp failing is contained: logged, non-zero exit, other camps still synced.

Commit once.

Step 11 of the approved design doc at `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`. Deploy `packages/clubspot-sync` as a scheduled Cloud Run job.

**Read the doc's "Authentication to Directus" and "GCP identity" sections first.** The auth section was rewritten two commits ago specifically for the post-#124 structure — the older description in this repo's history is wrong and cites files that no longer exist.

## Structure you are working in

There are now four Pulumi projects under `packages/infrastructure/src/`: `bootstrap/`, `infrastructure/`, `crm/`, and the shared non-project `directus/`. `just deploy` applies infrastructure then crm. #124 established the split; this session renamed its `people-hub` project to `crm`.

## Task

**1. The service account**, in `src/bootstrap/`. `src/bootstrap/report-runner.ts` is the model — read it. Identities live in the bootstrap stack, which is applied separately by `just deploy-bootstrap`. Use `ServiceAccount` from `../service-account` and its `allowImpersonation`.

Use `humanDeployer` from `src/config.ts` rather than hardcoding an address — `report-runner.ts:10` hardcodes a list, and the design doc explicitly says not to copy that.

Export it the way the others are, and make sure `src/infrastructure/identities.ts` can read it — that file is how the infrastructure project consumes bootstrap's identities across the stack boundary.

**2. The Directus token secret.** `randomSecret("clubspot-sync-directus-token")` in `src/infrastructure/directus.ts`, alongside `directusKey` / `directusSecret` / `directusDbPassword` (`:32-38`). Pulumi generates and owns the value; nothing is set out of band.

**3. `DirectusUser` gains an optional `token` input.** It currently takes `email`, `roleId`, `provider`, `externalIdentifier` (`src/directus/resources.ts:328-342`) and provisions OIDC users only. Add `token?: pulumi.Input<string>` and pass it through on **both** create and update. The machine user uses `provider: "default"` with no external identifier.

This is a change to a shared resource used by the existing `crm-staff-ungood` user — make it strictly additive so that user's behavior is unchanged when `token` is absent.

**4. The sync role and machine user**, in `src/infrastructure/directus-roles.ts`, beside Staff/Coach/Guardian. A `DirectusRole` named "Clubspot Sync", `appAccess: false`. Then export its policy id as a stack output from `src/infrastructure/index.ts` (`:25-27` shows the pattern), and read it in `src/crm/refs.ts` (`stringOutput`).

**5. The permission rules**, in `src/crm/index.ts` as `DirectusPermissionRule` resources — *not* on the role. They name collections, so they need the schema applied first; the role does not. That is #124's own rationale, stated in `directus-roles.ts:9-13`.

The doc's permission table is the spec. **The one that is easy to get wrong: `session_classes` needs `delete`**, unlike every other collection. The sync cancels rather than deletes everywhere else, but `session_classes` is a pure join with no status field, so a class a session no longer offers is removed outright (`DirectusClient.deleteItem`). A role without that permission passes review and then 403s the first time a session drops a class. Everything else is create/read/update only.

**6. The image and job.** A `clubspot-sync` target in the root `Dockerfile` — the existing `report-runner` target (`:13-17`) shows the `pnpm deploy --filter` pattern. Then a `gcp.cloudrunv2.Job` plus a `gcp.cloudscheduler.Job` in a new file under `src/infrastructure/`, modelled on `run-reports-job.ts`.

Environment for the job: `CLUBSPOT_CLUB_ID`, `DIRECTUS_URL`, and secrets `CLUBSPOT_EMAIL` / `CLUBSPOT_PASSWORD` / `DIRECTUS_TOKEN` via `secretKeyRef` (`run-reports-job.ts:82-98` is the shape). The Clubspot secrets already exist as `clubspot-username` / `clubspot-password`; grant the new service account access with `secret.grant(...)` rather than creating new secrets.

Set `buildOnPreview: false` on the image, as `run-reports-job.ts:42-43` now does — #114 is about exactly this, and a preview that rebuilds an image is the thing that issue exists to stop.

Pick a schedule that makes sense for a sync with a 24-hour refresh floor and say why in a comment. `run-reports-job.ts` runs hourly 9am–9pm PST; you do not have to match it.

## Scope fence

- Do NOT modify anything under `packages/clubspot-sync/src` or `test`. The application is done; this step deploys it.
- Do NOT modify `packages/crm/schema.yaml` or `docs/crm-schema.md`.
- Do NOT change the existing Staff/Coach/Guardian roles, their rules, `crm-staff-ungood`, or `run-reports-job.ts` beyond what is needed to read a shared value.
- Do NOT run `pulumi up`, `just deploy`, or `just deploy-bootstrap`. The human applies. `just preview` will not work either — the `crm` stack has not been initialized yet.
- Do NOT update `CLAUDE.md`'s package list — step 13.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes. That is the only automated gate available, since nothing can be applied from here.
- `tsc` accepts all four Pulumi projects.
- The `session_classes` delete permission is present.
- `DirectusUser` without a `token` behaves exactly as before.

Report the schedule you chose and anything the brief did not anticipate.

Commit once.
