Fix three duplicate Pulumi URNs introduced by the `clubspot-sync` infrastructure (commit `f56950e2`). Each aborts `pulumi up` at resource-registration time, before any diff is computed, so neither the `bootstrap` nor the `infrastructure` stack can currently apply. They were missed because the deploy step is deliberately deferred in this session.

All three are the same root cause: a resource name keyed on only one half of a pair.

## 1. `allowImpersonation` collides across service accounts

`packages/infrastructure/src/service-account.ts:18,24` names its two bindings `${member}-user` and `${member}-impersonator` — keyed on the member, with nothing identifying the service account.

`packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap/report-runner.ts:12` already grants `user:ungood@onetrue.name`. `packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap/clubspot-sync.ts:12` now grants the same member on a different account, in the same Pulumi project. Result: two resources named `user:ungood@onetrue.name-user`.

Fix by including the service account in the name. `ServiceAccount`'s constructor takes `accountId` as a plain string (`service-account.ts:6`), so it can be captured and used in a resource name — `this.name` cannot, since it is a `pulumi.Output`.

## 2. The Directus role and user share a name

`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus-roles.ts:75` (a `DirectusRole`) and `:88` (a `DirectusUser`) are both named `"crm-clubspot-sync"`. Both extend `pulumi.dynamic.Resource` without a custom `module`/`type`, so both register under the single type token `pulumi-nodejs:dynamic:Resource` — identical type, identical name, identical URN.

The existing pairs avoid this only by accident: `crm-staff` versus `crm-staff-ungood`. Rename the user to follow that shape.

## 3. `Secret.grant()` collides across grantees

`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/secret.ts:24` names the binding `secret-accessor-${this.plainId}` — keyed on the secret, not the grantee.

`run-reports-job.ts:26` grants `clubspot-username` and `clubspot-password` to `reportRunner`; `clubspot-sync-job.ts:22` grants the same two secrets to `clubspotSyncRunner`. Result: two resources named `secret-accessor-clubspot-username`, and two named `secret-accessor-clubspot-password`.

Reusing the existing secrets is correct and should stay — `grant()` simply cannot express two grantees today. Give it a way to. Note the member is a `pulumi.Input<string>` and may be an `Output`, so it cannot be interpolated into a resource name; the caller needs to supply a static label.

## Constraints

- **Renaming an existing resource means Pulumi deletes and recreates it.** That is acceptable here — these are IAM bindings, and recreation is harmless — but say so in the commit message so the first apply's diff isn't a surprise. Do not add `pulumi.Alias`; the user has explicitly declined aliasing for this work.
- Keep the fix to the naming. Do not change what any binding grants, to whom, or on what.
- `service-account.ts` and `secret.ts` are shared helpers used by existing resources. Update every call site.
- Do NOT touch `packages/clubspot-sync`, `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, or `docs/`.
- Do NOT run `pulumi up`, `just deploy`, or `just deploy-bootstrap`.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- No two resources in the same Pulumi project share a name, for `bootstrap`, `infrastructure`, and `crm`. Check this by reading the resource names each project registers, not by running Pulumi — you cannot apply from here.

input.prompt:
Fix four review findings in `packages/clubspot-sync`. All four are real bugs found by review of the session branch; three of them lose or corrupt data silently. The design doc is `.claude/plans/clubspot-directus-sync.md`.

## 1. Unbounded Parse queries silently truncate at 100 rows

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/main.ts:42` calls `queryCampEntries(camp).find()` with no limit. Parse's default page size is 100. Every other registration query in this repo sets it explicitly — `admin-functions/src/participants.ts:108`, `contacts.ts:60`, `sessions.ts:69` all use `.limit(1000)`.

**Failure:** a camp with 140 confirmed registrations syncs 100. No error is raised, the camp is logged `status: "ok"`, and its watermark advances — so the missing 40 are never retried. Silent, permanent.

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/camps.ts:10` (`discoverCamps`) and the other `find()` calls in `main.ts` have the same shape. Audit every `.find()` in the package and give each an explicit bound.

A hard cap that silently drops row 1001 is only a better failure than one that drops row 101. Decide whether to page or to fail loudly when a result hits the cap, and say which you chose and why. Do not leave a limit that can truncate without anyone noticing.

## 2. Medical data is write-once

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/person-sync.ts:154-171` reuses `fillGapsPatch` for `medical_profiles`, so only `null` columns are ever written.

Fill-gaps-only is deliberate for `people` — it protects a staff edit, and a merge, from being clobbered by the next registration naming that person. That rationale does **not** transfer to `medical_profiles`, where Clubspot is the sole source of truth and there is no competing staff edit to protect.

**Failure:** a participant syncs with `medical_allergies = "peanuts"`. The guardian later updates Clubspot to `"peanuts, bee stings"`. The CRM keeps `"peanuts"` indefinitely, and the roster staff read during an emergency is the stale one. A retracted medication is equally sticky.

Make `medical_profiles` track Clubspot, including clearing a value Clubspot no longer has. Use the same "no write when nothing changed" discipline as the plan functions — `diffFields` in `schedule.ts` is the existing helper for exactly that.

## 3. The participant's person is re-matched on every run

`person-sync.ts:43-56`'s `syncParticipant` runs the full matcher for every participant of every synced camp, then writes `contacts` and `medical_profiles` against whatever it resolves *now*. Nothing consults the existing registration's `person_id` — the column added precisely so identity resolves once.

`registrations.person_id` is correctly pinned on update (`registrations.ts:175-179`), which makes this worse rather than better: the two disagree.

**Failure:** "Jon Smith" (DOB 2012-05-01) syncs to person P1. Staff correct the spelling in Clubspot to "John". Next run `matchParticipant` requires an exact normalized first name, finds nothing, and creates P2. The medical profile and both guardian contacts are then written against P2, while the registration still points at P1. Staff open the registration, see the old name and no medical profile, while the fresh medical data sits on a person with no registrations.

The design doc's rule is that a person reference resolves **once, at creation, and is never re-resolved**. Honor it for participants the way it is already honored for `contacts` rows: if a `registrations` row already exists for this Clubspot registration, reuse its `person_id` and skip matching entirely.

This will mean the caller knows the existing registration before resolving the participant. Reordering the run loop in `sync-run.ts` is in scope.

## 4. The registration watermark is passed but dropped

`SyncGateway.fetchCampData(camp, watermark, until)` (`sync-run.ts:59`) is called with both bounds (`sync-run.ts:463`), but the only implementation, in `main.ts:30`, takes `(camp)` and ignores them. TypeScript cannot flag it — a narrower implementation is assignable.

`packages/clubspot-sync/README.md:67` and the design doc both state that registrations are filtered on `updatedAt` between the camp's watermark and the run start. They are not. Every synced camp re-reads and re-resolves every participant on every six-hour run.

Apply the bounds. `admin-functions/src/reports.ts:42` (`updatedBetween`) is the existing implementation of this exact filter. Note the interval is end-exclusive on purpose, so a write landing mid-run is picked up next time rather than skipped.

Make the signature mismatch impossible to reintroduce — an implementation that ignores a parameter should not typecheck as a valid gateway.

## Tests

Each fix needs one. In particular:
- A result at the query cap behaves the way you chose, and is covered.
- A changed medical value updates; an unchanged one writes nothing; a cleared one clears.
- A participant whose registration already exists reuses its `person_id` even when the matcher would now choose differently. This is the regression test for finding 3 — it must exist.
- The watermark bounds reach the Clubspot query.

## Scope fence

- `packages/clubspot-sync` only, plus `packages/clubspot-sync/README.md` if finding 4 changes what it should say.
- Do NOT change `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `docs/`, or anything under `packages/infrastructure`.
- Do NOT modify `packages/clubspot-sdk` or `packages/admin-functions`.
- Do NOT address the token/PII logging findings (`main.ts:87`, `directus.ts:118`) — those are a separate commit.
- Keep `fillGapsPatch`'s behavior for `people` exactly as it is. Only `medical_profiles` changes.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- No `.find()` in the package can truncate silently.
- A re-sync of an unchanged camp writes nothing.
- The person-reuse regression test passes, and fails if the reuse is removed.

Commit once.

### What the job syncs, and when

There is no config collection and no `enabled` toggle. The job syncs everything for one club. The
club id comes from a `CLUBSPOT_CLUB_ID` environment variable on the Cloud Run job, the same shape
as `CONFIG_SPREADSHEET_ID` today (`run-reports-job.ts:78`) and already an established variable name
in the SDK CLI (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/main.ts:128`).

Each run:

1. List every non-archived `Camp` for the club, as `camps.ts:37` already does.
2. For each camp, decide whether anything changed since that camp's own watermark. A camp's
   `updatedAt` does not move when a child object changes, so the camp is checked with one
   `Parse.Query.count()` per child class, each filtered on `updatedAt >= watermark`: `CampSession`,
   `CampClass`, `Registration`, and `RegistrationCampSession`. If every count is zero and the
   camp's own `updatedAt` is older than the watermark, skip the camp.
3. Sync each camp that changed, and record one log row per camp.

Two known holes in step 2, both closed by the same rule:

- `EntryCap` has no pointer to a camp (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts:338-342`), so a
  capacity-only change is invisible to the count queries.
- Nothing in Clubspot's `updatedAt` reveals a delete.

So any camp whose last successful sync is more than 24 hours old is synced regardless of the
counts. That is a refresh floor, not a snooze.

**Snooze is premature.** The cost the user is worried about is four `count()` calls per camp per
run. With tens of camps and an hourly schedule that is a few hundred cheap queries a day, against
the thousands of object reads a full pass costs. Add a snooze when a measurement says it is needed.

### The sync log

Not a missing secret — I checked. Every value on the VM is populated and correct:

```
OAUTH2_PROXY_GOOGLE_GROUP=all@cyccommunitysailing.org
OAUTH2_PROXY_GOOGLE_ADMIN_EMAIL=master@cyccommunitysailing.org
GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: 72 chars    GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET: 35 chars
OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECRET: 43 chars
```

All ten secrets exist, and the OAuth client credentials are demonstrably working — Google issued you a token. So it's not a secret, and it's not GCP IAM either.

**It's the Workspace domain-wide delegation entry for `substrate-runner@`.** That's the only link left in the chain, and `unauthorized_client` is precisely the error Google's token endpoint returns when a service account's client ID isn't authorized for the scopes it's asking for.

To check: **Admin → Security → API controls → Domain-wide delegation**, look for client ID **`115457003008765084595`** (that's `substrate-runner@`, distinct from the `115185692211855827749` you were looking at earlier).

Two possibilities, and I can't distinguish them from here:

1. **The entry is gone or was edited.** `docs/manual-setup.md` §5.2 has it checked off as done, and the portal used to work, so something changed. You were in that exact console page today — worth a look before assuming anything more exotic.

2. **The scope list is incomplete.** Here's the suggestive bit: `admin-scripts-runner@` holds **both** `admin.directory.group.readonly` *and* `admin.directory.user.readonly`, while §5.2 granted `substrate-runner@` only the group scope. Someone setting this up originally apparently found both were needed. oauth2-proxy's Google provider requests a user-directory scope alongside the group one in some versions, and the error's wording — *"or client not authorized for **any** of the scopes requested"* — is consistent with a partial grant failing the whole token request.

So: confirm the entry exists, and grant **both** scopes. That matches the working precedent and costs nothing extra, since both are read-only.

Worth stating plainly: none of this is my session's doing. Nothing from this branch has been applied, and the containers have been up 3 days without a restart — the config on that VM predates today's work entirely.

Fix two disclosure findings from review of `packages/clubspot-sync`. Both write sensitive data into Cloud Logging, where it outlives the run and is readable by anyone with log access.

## 1. The Directus static token is logged at debug level

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/main.ts:87-90`'s `preAction` hook logs `options: action.opts()`, which dumps every resolved option. That now includes `--directus-token` and `--password`.

The pattern was copied from `packages/admin-functions/src/main.ts:42`, where it was already questionable, but the Directus static token is new and worse: it is long-lived, it is Pulumi-generated, and rotating it means a Pulumi apply. One `--verbose debug` run in Cloud Run puts it in the log permanently.

CLAUDE.md and #49 both record that secrets must not be exposed this way. Keep the debug line — knowing which action ran with which options is genuinely useful — but redact the secret-bearing options rather than dropping the log entirely.

Do NOT change `admin-functions/src/main.ts`. It has the same shape and the same problem, but it is out of scope here; report it and I will file an issue.

## 2. Dry-run logs a minor's medical record

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/directus.ts:118` logs the whole `patch` in `updateItem`'s dry-run branch. For `medical_profiles` that is `conditions`, `allergies`, `medications`, and physician contact.

The design doc's own rollout step is "the first production run is a dry run" — so the recommended first action writes minors' medical data to stderr and Cloud Logging, entirely outside the permission model `medical_profiles` exists to enforce.

`createItems` already gets this right: it logs a collection and a count, no values (`directus.ts:109`). `deleteItem` logs an id, which is fine. Make `updateItem` consistent with `createItems`.

A dry run still has to be useful for verifying what would change, so log enough to audit — the collection, the row id, and which fields would be written — without the values themselves. Field *names* are schema, not data.

## Scope fence

- `packages/clubspot-sync/src/main.ts` and `src/directus.ts` only, plus tests.
- Do NOT modify `packages/admin-functions`.
- Do NOT change what is written to Directus, only what is logged.
- Do NOT touch the plan functions, `person-sync.ts`, `sync-run.ts`, or `packages/infrastructure`.

## Tests

- The debug log does not contain the token or the Clubspot password.
- A dry-run `updateItem` on `medical_profiles` logs the field names but none of the values.

The existing tests stub `fetch` and are in `packages/clubspot-sync/test/`. For the logging assertions, spy on winston rather than reaching into transports.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- Grepping the package for a log call that passes a whole options object or a whole patch turns up nothing.

Commit once.

input.description: Replace refresh floor with backoff
input.prompt:
Act on a PR review comment on #128. The reviewer (the repo owner) said, on `packages/clubspot-sync/src/change-detection.ts:62`:

> I don't really like this change detection mechanism, as a) most of the work is in querying clubspot, which has to be done to get the childCounts anyway and b) it will continue to sync a camp indefinitely at least once a day.
>
> Instead, I want an exponential backoff approach: start by syncing every time the job runs, but if there are no changes for a particular entity being synced - backoff by some reasonable percent - to a maximum of once a week.

The design doc's "What the job syncs, and when" section has been rewritten to match; read it — it is the specification.

## What goes away

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/change-detection.ts` in its current form. Both halves of it are wrong:

- `countChildChanges` issues four `Parse.Query.count()` calls per camp per run, hitting the same classes a sync would read anyway. They cost about what fetching costs and buy almost nothing.
- `needsSync`'s `REFRESH_FLOOR_MS` forces a full sync of every camp every 24 hours, so a camp that finished in 2024 and can never change again is resynced daily, forever.

Delete both, and the `watermarkForCamp` plumbing if the backoff replaces its role. Their tests go with them.

## What replaces it

Per-camp exponential backoff, decided from the sync log:

- A camp starts syncing on every run.
- A sync that writes nothing backs the camp off — roughly doubling its interval.
- A sync that writes something resets it to every run.
- The interval caps at one week.

**No schema change.** `sync_program_runs` already records `items_created` and `items_updated` per camp per run, so "how many consecutive runs wrote nothing" is a read of the log the run loop already performs (`sync-run.ts` reads prior program runs once per run). The interval is a function of that count; a camp is due when `now - last_sync_start >= interval`.

Keep the decision a **pure function over plain data**, the way `needsSync` was — that is the one thing about the old design worth preserving. Something like "given this camp's ordered prior runs and this clock, is it due, and what is its interval". The executor stays thin.

Pick the base interval, the growth factor, and how you count a "wrote nothing" run, and justify each in a short comment. The job runs every six hours; the cap is one week. Note that `skipped` rows are not sync attempts and must not count as either changed or unchanged — only actual syncs move the backoff.

## Two things this simplifies — verify, don't assume

The old design had a "two known holes" note, both papered over by the refresh floor:

- `EntryCap` has no pointer to a camp, so a capacity-only change was invisible to the count queries.
- Nothing in Clubspot's `updatedAt` reveals a delete.

Neither should matter now, because a due run is a full reconcile of the camp's schedule rather than something that must detect a change first. Confirm that is actually true of the current code — that a due camp re-reads and reconciles sessions, classes, session_classes and entry caps unconditionally — rather than taking it on faith. If some part of the sync still depends on change detection having happened, say so.

## Interaction with the registration watermark

Registrations are still filtered on `updatedAt` between the camp's watermark and the run start — that is separate from the backoff and stays. Make sure the watermark still advances correctly when a camp is synced after a long backoff: the window must cover everything since the last *successful* sync, not since the last run.

This is the subtle one. A camp backed off to weekly that then syncs must not miss registrations created during the backoff.

## Tests

- A camp with no prior runs is due.
- A camp whose last sync wrote something is due on the next run.
- Consecutive zero-write syncs lengthen the interval.
- The interval never exceeds a week.
- A sync that writes something resets the interval.
- `skipped` rows do not affect the backoff.
- A camp synced after a long backoff uses a watermark covering the whole gap.

## Scope fence

- `packages/clubspot-sync` only, plus `packages/clubspot-sync/README.md` (it documents the 24-hour refresh floor, which is going away).
- Do NOT change `packages/crm`, `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `docs/`, or `packages/infrastructure`. The backoff needs no new column — if you conclude it does, stop and report rather than changing the schema.
- Do NOT change the Cloud Run schedule.
- Do NOT touch `packages/clubspot-sdk` or `packages/admin-functions`.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- No `Parse.Query.count()` remains in the package.
- The backoff decision is a pure function with direct unit tests.
- A camp that syncs and writes nothing is not synced again on the very next run.

Report the base interval and factor you chose, and whether the two "known holes" really are closed.

Commit once.

Four items: three review findings from PR #128, plus a CLI gap the repo owner asked for.

## 1. `registration_entries.status` escapes its documented vocabulary

`packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts`'s `calculateEntryStatus` (around `:87-95`) folds Clubspot's precedence — archived wins, then waitlist — and otherwise returns `Registration.status` **raw**.

`docs/crm-schema.md` documents `registration_entries.status` as `enum (confirmed, waitlist, cancelled)`, and `packages/crm/schema.yaml` configures the field as a three-choice `select-dropdown`.

`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/queries.ts:9`'s `queryCampEntries` filters only on `.exists("confirmed_at")`, so an `applied` or `invited` registration reaches the mapping (see `queries.ts:32`, which lists `confirmed`, `applied`, `invited` as real values). Those write `status: "applied"` — accepted by the varchar column, blank in the Directus dropdown, and invisible to any roster filter written against the three documented values. A registration with no `status` at all writes `""` into a NOT NULL column.

Normalize to the three documented values with an explicit mapping, and **log a warning for anything unmapped rather than writing it through**. An unrecognized status is a signal that Clubspot grew a value we do not understand; it should be visible, not silently persisted.

**Do NOT change `packages/crm/schema.yaml` or the documented vocabulary.** Adding a fourth value means regenerating the snapshot against a live Directus, which is a whole step. If you conclude the vocabulary genuinely needs a fourth value, stop and report instead.

## 2. `registration_billing` can fail a camp permanently

`registrations.ts` (around `:264-276`) reconciles billing by `clubspot_billing_id`, but `packages/crm/schema.yaml` makes `registration_billing.registration_id` unique — one billing row per registration.

If Clubspot ever replaces a registration's billing object, the new object has a new id, so the plan emits a **create**, and Directus rejects it on the `registration_id` unique constraint. That camp then fails on every subsequent run.

Reconcile on `registration_id` instead — it is the actual 1:1 key, and it is what the uniqueness constraint enforces. `clubspot_billing_id` becomes a tracked field rather than the match key.

## 3. `admin-functions` logs the Clubspot password

`packages/admin-functions/src/main.ts:42`'s `preAction` hook logs `options: action.opts()`, which includes `--password`. This is pre-existing — it predates the sync work — but it is the same bug just fixed in `packages/clubspot-sync/src/main.ts`, and CLAUDE.md and #49 both record that secrets must not be exposed this way.

Apply the same treatment. `clubspot-sync`'s `redactSecrets` is the model. Do not extract a shared helper for it — `commodore` is explicitly not a kitchen-sink package (that is settled in #122), and duplicating a six-line redaction is cheaper than the dependency argument.

## 4. A CLI path for verifying and backfilling one camp

The repo owner wants to "sync a single camp, so I can manually verify and backfill old camps."

`--camp <id>` already exists and correctly bypasses the backoff (`sync-run.ts:471`). What is missing is the backfill half: `watermarkForCamp` still bounds the registration query to "since this camp's last successful sync", so re-running `--camp` on an already-synced camp picks up only recent changes. For a backfill — say after a mapping fix — that reads nothing and looks like success.

Add a way to ignore the watermark and re-read a camp's registrations in full. Name and shape are yours; `--full` and `--since <iso>` are both reasonable, and `--since` is more useful for a partial backfill. It must compose with `--camp`, and it must be obvious from `--help` what it does.

Two things to get right:
- A full backfill must not corrupt the watermark for normal runs. Think about what gets written to `sync_program_runs` and whether a backfill should advance the watermark at all.
- It must be safe to combine with `--dry-run`, since that is how someone would check a backfill before committing to it.

Update `packages/clubspot-sync/README.md` to document the backfill path — that is the thing a human reaches for months from now.

## Scope fence

- `packages/clubspot-sync` and the one function in `packages/admin-functions/src/main.ts`.
- Do NOT change `packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `packages/crm/src`, `docs/`, or `packages/infrastructure`.
- Do NOT change the backoff logic, person matching, or the plan functions beyond items 1 and 2.
- Do NOT touch `packages/clubspot-sdk`.

## Tests

- An `applied` status maps to a documented value and warns; an unmapped status warns rather than being written.
- A registration with no status does not write `""`.
- A replaced billing object updates the existing row rather than emitting a create.
- The backfill flag widens the registration window, and composes with `--camp` and `--dry-run`.
- `admin-functions`' debug log does not contain the password.

## Acceptance

- `just ci` passes.
- `node packages/clubspot-sync/dist/main.js --help` shows the backfill option.
- No code path writes a `registration_entries.status` outside the three documented values.

Report the backfill flag you chose and how you decided the watermark question.

Commit once.

content.text:

The gap is the backfill half. `watermarkForCamp` bounds the registration query to "since this camp's last successful sync," so re-running `--camp` on a camp that's already been synced reads only what changed since — which, after a mapping fix, is nothing. It would complete, report `ok`, and write nothing, looking for all the world like success. So I asked for a way to ignore the watermark, composable with `--camp` and `--dry-run`.

**Error 1 is #124's latent bug, surfacing because #124 was never applied.** Only two files in the whole package use an `/index.js` suffix — `directus-roles.ts:1` and `crm/index.ts:11`, both from #124. content.text:
First deploy attempt failed. Two causes, and one of them was my mistake.

**#124's code had never actually been run.** `directus-roles.ts:1` and `crm/index.ts:11` imported `"../directus/index.js"` — the only two imports in the package carrying a `.js` suffix. Pulumi runs the program through its vendored ts-node in **CommonJS** mode, which resolves that path literally, and only `index.ts` exists on disk. The stack died with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` before computing a diff. That came in with #124 and nothing had exercised it, since its apply was deliberately held. Fixed in `17827f68`.

**I skipped `just deploy-bootstrap`.** The new `clubspot-sync` service account lives in the bootstrap stack, and `just deploy` only applies infrastructure and crm. So `identities.ts:30` read an output that didn't exist yet and crashed on `undefined.email`. The design doc says this explicitly and I went straight to `just deploy` anyway.

Bootstrap is now applied — 7 created, 4 deleted, matching the IAM renames. Main deploy is running.

One thing worth fixing afterwards: `identities.ts:20` uses `getOutput`, so a missing stack output surfaces as `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'email')`. `crm/refs.ts:14` already uses `requireOutput` for exactly this reason, with a comment saying so — it fails naming the output instead. Worth making `identities.ts` match, since that error cost more to diagnose than it should have.

from pathlib import Path

f = Path("packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/clubspot-sync-job.ts")
s = f.read_text()
s = s.replace('new docker.Image(\n  "clubspot-sync-image",', 'const clubspotSyncImage = new docker.Image(\n  "clubspot-sync-image",', 1)
old = "  { dependsOn: [runApi] },"
